historical_record.description: Built for the Chronicle's publisher Michael H. de Young, who wanted the tallest building he could get, to designs by Burnham & Root: a nine-storey steel-framed skyscraper faced in brownstone at street level and pressed brick and terra cotta above, in a conservative Richardsonian Romanesque, with a clock tower.
The Chronicle Building's four-story clock tower burned after skyrockets set it alight during a mayoral victory parade.

Gutted in the 1906 fire before the enlargement was finished, the building was rebuilt largely to Burnham's 1905 plans: the 1905 annex was repaired, the original section reconstructed, the two Geary Street bays rebuilt from the ground, and the clock tower left off. It was the Chronicle's headquarters until the paper moved to 901 Mission Street in 1924.
The Chronicle moved out of the building to Fifth and Mission Streets.
The Filipino Federation of America was headquartered here in 1946.
Home Mutual Savings & Loan covered the brick and stone façade with white enamel panels.
A 16-story office building stood at the property.

The City Planning Commission adopted the CEQA findings and mitigated negative declaration for the proposed eight-story vertical addition, historic facade restoration, and conversion of the existing office building to a mixed-use project.
The City Planning Commission determined that the net new shadow impact on Union Square Park from the proposed addition is not adverse.
The City Planning Commission approved a resolution recommending to the Board of Supervisors a General Plan amendment to change the height and bulk district of the site.

The City Planning Commission approved the Determination of Compliance under Section 309 to permit the eight-story vertical addition, historic facade restoration, and conversion to a mixed-use project, subject to the granting of a variance for bay windows projecting over the property at 88 Kearny Street.
The City Planning Commission approved conditional use authorization to allow a hotel in the C-3-0 Downtown Office Zoning District.

The City Planning Commission approved a resolution recommending to the Board of Supervisors the approval of the creation of the Downtown Housing Demonstration Special Use District encompassing the subject property.
The City Planning Commission approved resolutions recommending to the Board of Supervisors the conditional designation of the property as San Francisco Landmark No. 243.
The City Planning Commission approved a resolution recommending to the Board of Supervisors the conditional approval of a Mills Act Historical Property Contract for the subject property.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 243, Chronicle Building.
